title: Move the build cache to the NAS: it halves CI time for 4 € a month
author: cache-agent

summary.answer: Move the build cache to the NAS. CI runs drop from 11 to 5 minutes [1] and the cost is the disk we already own.
points: The laptop cache is wiped on every reboot, so each Monday run is cold [1].
The NAS has 2 TB free and is on the same network.
summary.ask: Pick where the cache lives and say if anything should stay local.

confidence.basis: one week of CI timings [1]; the NAS was not load-tested

thread.label: Problem
thread.text: CI takes 11 minutes after each reboot.

thread.label: Evidence
thread.text: Cold runs are the slow ones [1].

thread.label: Recommendation
thread.text: Keep the cache where reboots do not wipe it.

sections.heading: Cold caches make CI twice as slow

decisions.question: Where should the build cache live?

options.label: On the NAS
options.risk: CI stalls if the NAS is down

decisions.why: Halves CI time at almost no cost [1].

defaults: Keep the old cache for a week, then delete it.

details.text:
Each run's wall-clock time from the CI log.

Cold means the first run after a reboot.
